citation: "First Presbyterian Church. Indiana Avenue and Twenty-First Street (1912)." Halftone plate facing p. 76 in Philo Adams Otis, The First Presbyterian Church, 1833-1913: A History of the Oldest Organization in Chicago (Chicago: Fleming H. Revell, 1913).
author: Philo Adams Otis (compiler); photographer not named
describes_date: 1912 (the photograph, as its caption dates it); the church as finished about 1872-1873
repository: Internet Archive, item firstpreschurch00otis (scanned from a library copy).
locator: Scan leaf n116, the plate captioned 'FIRST PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH. Indiana Avenue and Twenty-First Street (1912).' The whole plate: the church's south-west tower and spire, the west gable seen edge-on, and the nave's south roof slope to the east gable, from Indiana Avenue south of 21st Street; in front, the two-storey brick building with a billboard and a small gabled house across 21st Street, a streetcar, and the row houses on Indiana Avenue north of the church.
rights_note: A photograph published in a book in the United States in 1913, in the public domain. Read for forms, counts and proportions; no texture or mesh is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-24 from the Internet Archive's page image https://archive.org/download/firstpreschurch00otis/page/n116.jpg (2247 x 3630 px, sha256 d772ea7d8d116194da3728a10c8084119cdd88dd0f58589767970e19418d1754); the plate inside its printed border (page px 278-1902 x 598-2932) is committed, scaled to 1050 x 1509 px and greyscale, as data/sources/assets/first_presbyterian_2029_otis_t3104/otis_1913_plate_1912.jpg (T-3104).
note: Taken twenty-five years after the book's 1887 plate (otis_1913_first_presbyterian_21st_indiana_1887) and some months before the last service of 29 December 1912. The camera stood in Indiana Avenue's roadway about 66 m south of 21st Street and looked north-north-east, tilted up about 17.5 degrees to take in the spire, so the tower's verticals lean and the spire is foreshortened (the camera is solved in data/reference_views/first_presbyterian_church_2029_indiana/otis_1913_plate_1912.json). It shows the tower's south face in light and its west face in shade, the tower's three stages, gablets, corner pinnacles and plain octagonal slated spire to its knob and rod; the west gable edge-on, its coping and the tall cross at its apex; the nave's south slope, slated, with two gabled ventilators, and the east gable with a short stack at its apex. The 21st Street flank does not show: the buildings on 21st Street's south side and the streetcar on Indiana Avenue screen it below the eaves. A tall stack rising beyond the east gable lines up with the left end of the frame building in the right foreground and cannot be placed from one view.
what_it_supplies: a second camera on the tower and spire, which agree with the 1887 plate's heights within the halftone's reading
the nave's south roof slope: its two gabled ventilators and the stack on the east gable's apex
the height of the west gable's cross, which it reads as the 1887 plate does once that plate's crossbar is not taken for its top
what_it_does_not_supply: the 21st Street flank's walls, buttresses and openings, screened by the buildings across 21st Street and the streetcar
the north slope and the north and east walls
the spire's band of lucarnes, too small to resolve in the halftone at this distance
